claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm enquiring about my son Alex. He's 17 years old and lives with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. It's helpful to know he's 17 and lives with you in Manchester.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask: is he currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England

Or has Alex left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's left education actually. He finished school and now he's working full-time at the local warehouse.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I just need to check a couple more things to give you an accurate assessment.

When did Alex leave education? Specifically, was it:
- At the end of the summer term (around June/July), or
- At a different time during the school year?

This is important because there can be a period after leaving education where Child Benefit may still be payable.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left at the end of the summer term, back in June. He went straight into work after that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

Which year did Alex leave education - was it June 2024, or an earlier year?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was June 2024, so just a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Let me ask one more important question:

After Alex left education in June 2024, did he register with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), or
- The armed services?

This is relevant because if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with one of these services, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he didn't register with either of those. He just went straight into the warehouse job after finishing school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He left approved education at the end of the summer term in June 2024
- He went straight into full-time work (24+ hours per week at a warehouse)
- He did not register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Child Benefit for children aged 16 or over** normally only continues if the child stays in approved education or training.
- **When a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week** and is no longer in approved education or training, Child Benefit stops.
- While there is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, Alex did not take this step.

Since Alex left school in June 2024 and went straight into full-time work at the warehouse without registering with the relevant services, your eligibility for Child Benefit for him has ended.

If you have any questions or if Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he returns to approved education or training), please don't hesitate to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
